solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sort out stylish clothing provided

indicators.note: clothing wraps around a body, so one word is dressed around the other

parts.note: stylish and elegant
provided that, on condition

explanation.surface: An instruction to tidy up some fashionable clothes, provided there are any.
explanation.definitionFit: To classify things is to arrange them into groups, a synonym of sorting them out.

clue.text: Broadcast vulgar programme for students

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard rather than seen, so the sound counts

parts.note: coarse means crude or vulgar

explanation.surface: Complaining that a crude programme has been aired to students.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' and 'programme' suggest television; programme is the study sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A course is a planned series of lessons or study taken by students.

clue.text: Maintain a sizeable lock-up

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a tress is a long lock of hair

explanation.surface: Keeping up a big prison lock-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock-up' reads as a jail; the hyphen hides lock (of hair) plus the up signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain a claim is to assert it, insisting it is true.

clue.text: Drink and a snack following ramble

indicators.note: following puts the snack piece after the walking piece

parts.note: to snake is to meander or wind about
a bite to eat is a snack

explanation.surface: A pub stop for a drink and a bite to eat after a country walk.
explanation.walkthrough: A snakebite is a British pub drink of lager mixed with cider.
explanation.definitionFit: Snakebite is the name of a mixed drink of lager and cider, an alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Lace if under a petticoat can be a revealing thing

indicators.note: to lace a drink is to spike or mix it, so the letters are blended

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
a slip is a petticoat or underskirt

explanation.surface: Lace showing beneath a petticoat could reveal more than intended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lace' looks like the fabric, but it is the mixing verb; the petticoat itself is a straight synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A Freudian slip is an unintentional error of speech thought to expose a hidden wish.

clue.text: Prepare crumble to go round cakes

indicators.note: going round turns the pair of words back to front, so they are read from the end

parts.note: to set something up is to prepare it
to rot is to decay and crumble away

explanation.surface: A baking instruction: make a crumble topping to go around some cakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prepare crumble' reads like a pudding recipe, but the two words each become a short verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Tortes are rich layered cakes of Central European style, so the plural matches the plural definition.

clue.text: Begins work on measurements for printers

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
an en is a printer's unit of width

explanation.surface: Someone starts work on measurements for a print shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Opens means starts or commences, as a play or meeting does.

clue.text: Bit of cereal found in red wine? That's rubbish!

definitions.note: rubbish as a verb: to criticise harshly

indicators.note: something found in another sits inside it

parts.note: vino tinto is Spanish for red wine
an ear of wheat or corn is part of the plant

explanation.surface: A diner finds a bit of cereal in the red wine and complains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish' looks like a scornful exclamation, but it is the verb meaning to criticise.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear into someone is to attack them verbally, just as to rubbish them is to disparage.

clue.text: Farm animals, regularly handled in this enclosure

parts.note: livestock, the animals kept on a farm

indicators.note: regularly means at fixed intervals, so every second letter is taken

parts.note: the even letters of handled

explanation.surface: Farm animals are routinely handled inside this pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockade is a defensive enclosure or barrier made of upright stakes.

clue.text: Some nuns have nasal whiskers to deal with?

definitions.note: a cryptic description: an unshaven face has whiskers needing attention

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following words are used, a run straddling them

parts.note: the run starts inside the first word and ends at the start of the third

explanation.surface: A comic image of nuns sprouting whiskers from their noses that need dealing with.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unshaven has stubble left on the face, whiskers still to be removed, so the question mark flags a descriptive definition.

clue.text: Smooth representative lacks energy — getting old

indicators.note: something that lacks a thing goes without it, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a legate is an envoy or papal representative
E is the physics symbol for energy
O is a standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A tired delegate with no energy left is getting on in years.
explanation.walkthrough: The final E of the envoy word is the energy that is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Legato is the musical direction to play notes smoothly and connected, without breaks between them.

clue.text: One causing inflation with some money for bread

parts.note: a pumper pumps up tyres or balloons
a nickel is a US five-cent coin

explanation.surface: An economist blaming whoever pushes up prices, with money for bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inflation' and 'money' suggest economics, and 'bread' is slang for money; all three are literal here.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumpernickel is a dark, dense German rye bread.

clue.text: Assist old golfer carrying putter at the finish

indicators.note: one carrying something holds it inside

parts.note: Seve Ballesteros, the Spanish golf champion who died in 2011

indicators.note: the finish of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the final letter of putter

explanation.surface: A caddie helping a veteran golfer who is carrying his putter to the end of the round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putter' looks like the golf club in the surface; only its last letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: To serve someone is to work for them or help them, a synonym of assist.

clue.text: Joint put behind tap

indicators.note: behind says the second word comes after the first one in the answer

parts.note: to drum is to tap repeatedly
to stick something somewhere is to put it there

explanation.surface: Plumbing or carpentry advice about placing a joint behind a tap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' and 'tap' suggest pipework; the joint is actually a cut of poultry.
explanation.definitionFit: A drumstick is the lower leg of a cooked chicken or turkey, a joint of meat.

clue.text: Upset girl's been chosen

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, with the possessive S
appointed means selected for a post

explanation.surface: A girl is upset that she has been picked for something.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface implies the girl is upset; the answer is the upset itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Disappointed means let down or saddened, an adjective sense of upset.

clue.text: Sadly one trainee beginning to booze gets drunk

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone badly wrong, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of booze

explanation.surface: A trainee who starts drinking ends up drunk, sadly.
explanation.definitionFit: An inebriate is a person who is habitually intoxicated, the noun sense of a drunk.

clue.text: Gossip when buffet and tea are served in court

indicators.note: things served in a place are placed inside it

parts.note: CT is the abbreviation for court
to buffet is to strike
cha is a slang word for tea

explanation.surface: Idle talk at court while a buffet and tea are laid on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buffet' looks like a spread of food; it is the verb meaning to strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Chitchat is light informal conversation, much like gossip or small talk.

clue.text: Nosey type taking in young male inmate

indicators.note: taking in means absorbing something inside

parts.note: a prier is someone who pries
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: A nosy person befriends a young male inmate.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner is a person held in jail, which is what an inmate is.

clue.text: Theatres rely on private health here

parts.note: the twelve letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Operating theatres depend on paying patients in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no separate anagram signal: the setter leaves the solver to spot that the two opening words rearrange. HARLEY STREET is the London street famous for private doctors' practices.
explanation.definitionFit: Harley Street in central London is lined with private medical clinics, so it is where private health care is found.

clue.text: Put wise students here?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to tell or advise someone
second meaning, split in two words: where pupils sit, in a school class

explanation.surface: Should one enlighten the students in this place?
explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning splits the answer into IN FORM; a form is a British school class.
explanation.definitionFit: To inform someone is to tell them facts; in form describes pupils sitting in their class.

clue.text: Save damaged retina

indicators.note: something damaged is broken up and out of its proper order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A plea to rescue an injured eye.
explanation.definitionFit: To retain something is to keep it rather than lose it, which is one sense of save.

clue.text: I sanction changing conductor

indicators.note: changing the letters means altering their order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone in authority approves a change of conductor.
explanation.definitionFit: Arturo Toscanini was a celebrated Italian orchestral conductor of the twentieth century.

clue.text: American land found in sea passage

parts.note: A is a common abbreviation for American
an isle is land surrounded by sea

explanation.surface: An American territory discovered in a sea passage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sea passage' reads as a strait, but sea belongs to the island description.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a walkway between rows of seats, a passage.

clue.text: Managed, say, flipping 1 across

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it the other way round

parts.note: e.g. means for example, as does say

explanation.surface: Someone managed, for example, to flip over the first answer.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer to 1 across, CLASSIFY.
explanation.definitionFit: To range items is to arrange them in rows or classes, so it can stand for classify.

clue.text: Polish street behind this square

indicators.note: behind this says the next piece follows the one just given

parts.note: to hone a blade is to sharpen or polish it
ST is the usual abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Instructions to polish a street that lies behind a town square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality, and 'square' like a plaza; it is a verb, and the definition is the old slang for fair dealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Square in the informal sense of fair and upright, as in a square deal, matches truthful and fair.

clue.text: Musical cellist is after satisfactory note at heart of show

indicators.note: is after places the last piece at the end, following the others

parts.note: OK means acceptable or satisfactory
la is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, so its central letters are taken

parts.note: the two central letters of show
Yo-Yo Ma is the famous cellist

explanation.surface: A musician reviewing a show says the cellist was satisfactory.
explanation.walkthrough: The cellist is Yo-Yo Ma, whose short surname the setter uses.
explanation.definitionFit: Oklahoma! is the 1943 Rodgers and Hammerstein stage musical.

clue.text: Heartless old warden gets the bird!

indicators.note: without a heart, the central letter of the word is taken out

parts.note: turnkey is an old word for a jailer who keeps the keys

explanation.surface: A cruel prison guard of the past is booed off: he gets the bird.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'get the bird' is British slang for being jeered; here bird is simply the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The turkey is a large farmyard bird, eaten at Christmas and Thanksgiving.

clue.text: Civic dignitary put tree on island

parts.note: the alder is a tree of damp ground
the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A local councillor plants a tree on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: An alderman is a senior member of a borough or city council, a civic office holder.
